allMaps.title: All Maps
allMaps.zoomSyncAllTooltip: Zoom stays in sync: every map — tiles and the composite overlay — moves together.
allMaps.zoomSyncSingleTooltip: Zoom each map on its own: only the map under the cursor changes.
allMaps.zoomHint: Ctrl + wheel = zoom · drag = pan · double-click = reset
allMaps.tileSizeTooltip: Minimum tile width: {{value}} px (grid reflows to fit)
allMaps.empty: No maps available — open a file with EDS or pattern data.

quantify.title: Pixel Quantification
quantify.copyTooltip: Copy quantification to clipboard (tab-separated for Excel)

regionAvg.title: Region Average
regionAvg.description: Average composition (mean ± σ per element) over a rectangular block of pixels. Use it to measure a grain or a precipitate without picking individual pixels — pick the bounding rows and columns below.
regionAvg.computeTooltip: Sum every pixel in the rectangle, return per-element mean and standard deviation. The single-pixel quantifier above gives you one row's worth of data; this one gives you a whole region's.
regionAvg.copyTooltip: Copy region quantification to clipboard (tab-separated for Excel)

suggest.title: Phase Suggestion
suggest.description: Suggests crystal phases based on At.% at current pixel coordinates.
suggest.sourceCifTooltip: Matching against your curated CIF library (Database/crystal_database.xlsx).
suggest.sourceDefaultTooltip: No CIF database built yet — falling back to a hardcoded library of common phases. Build the database for better matches.
suggest.none: No phases suggested for this composition.
suggest.atPixelTooltip: The pixel these suggestions were computed for. Clicking another pixel on the map updates them.
suggest.staleHint: Showing an older pixel — press “Suggest Phases” for ({{row}}, {{col}}).
suggest.elementTooltip: {{el}}: measured {{measured}} at%, this phase expects {{expected}} at%. An element the phase needs but the pixel lacks is what rules it out.
suggest.thisPixelAlone: This pixel alone — the map decides by composition group:

swipe.handleTooltip: Drag to slide the A/B split

threshold.convertToMaskTooltip: Create a mask layer from this threshold (gates layers below via multiply blend)

phaseMap.title: Phase Map Builder
phaseMap.minScoreTooltip: Pixels below this match score are left unclassified
phaseMap.autoClassifyTooltip: Match every pixel against the curated CIF library
phaseMap.noMapHintPost: to assign each pixel its closest CIF phase.
phaseMap.canvasPolygonTooltip: Click to add a vertex; close with the Close polygon button
phaseMap.canvasRectTooltip: Click to inspect, drag to select a region
phaseMap.readout: Pixel ({{row}}, {{col}}) — drag a rectangle to paint a region, click a legend phase to assign it.
phaseMap.assignRegionTooltipNoPhase: Pick a phase from the legend first
phaseMap.polygonHint: Click on the map to add vertices ({{count}} placed{{suffix}}).
phaseMap.closeAssignTooltipNoPhase: Pick a phase from the legend first
phaseMap.closeAssignTooltipNeedMore: Need at least 3 vertices to form a polygon
phaseMap.closeAssignTooltip: Close & assign polygon ({{count}} vertices) to phase #{{phase}}
phaseMap.sendToIndexingTooltip: Send phase classification to the Indexing module so each phase is tested only on its assigned pixels
phaseMap.modeTooltip: Clusters: group pixels of similar composition and match each group's mean — more reliable, because a single pixel's composition carries several at% of measurement error. Per pixel: match every pixel on its own.
phaseMap.nClustersTooltip: Number of composition groups. Leave on auto and it is chosen by the spatial coherence of the resulting map.
phaseMap.phaseSelectionTooltip: Untick a phase to keep it out of the classification. Useful when two library entries are chemically indistinguishable.
phaseMap.ambiguousTooltip: Another phase from a different group scored within 0.01 — chemistry cannot separate them here.
phaseMap.undoTooltip: Take back the last change ({{what}}). One level.
phaseMap.replaceTooltip: Repoint every pixel of one phase at another. For a classifier error that covers a large part of the map, where selecting by hand is not practical.
phaseMap.replaceGo: Replace every pixel of that phase with the one selected in the legend
phaseMap.replaceNeedTarget: Pick the target phase in the legend first
phaseMap.replaceHint: Target is whichever phase is selected in the legend.
phaseMap.colorTooltip: Click to recolour {{name}}, right-click to reset. The colour is shared with the EBSD phase map.
phaseMap.colorHint: Click a swatch to recolour · right-click resets

hoverTips.regionColEnd: Last column of the averaging rectangle (inclusive)

hoverTips.minScoreSlider: Drag to set the minimum match score for a pixel to be classified
hoverTips.paintModeRectangle: Paint regions by dragging an axis-aligned rectangle
hoverTips.paintModePolygon: Paint regions by clicking polygon vertices
hoverTips.colorInput: Pick a new display color for this element
hoverTips.resetColors: Reset all element colors to their defaults

wand.modeTooltip: Click a feature to select everything chemically like it, then set how far the selection reaches.
wand.hint: Click a feature on the map to select it.
wand.sliderTooltip: How far the selection reaches. The axis is the pixel count, because thresholding the chemistry directly has dead bands. A sudden jump means the selection has escaped into the matrix.
wand.enrichmentTooltip: How many times the map's own background level each element reaches in this selection. Below about 1.3x the classifier itself cannot tell feature from background.
wand.assignTooltip: Assign the selected phase to these pixels
wand.assignTooltipNoPhase: Pick a phase from the legend first
wand.scopeConnectedTooltip: Grow outward from the pixel you clicked, stopping at the feature's edge.
wand.scopeAllTooltip: Select every pixel on the map with a similar composition, not just this one feature. A phase is rarely a single blob.

structures.viewStructuresTooltip: What the map is made of: pixels grouped by element ratio alone, before anything is named.
structures.viewPhasesTooltip: The same map seen through the names you gave the structures.
structures.none: This map has no structures. Re-run the classification in “Clusters” mode.
structures.unnamed: not named yet — pick a phase below
structures.scaleTooltip: How far the composition is averaged before grouping. Larger gives cleaner regions but absorbs features thinner than the box. Off reproduces the old behaviour: measured at 8 structures on SampleB it left 3491 pieces with a median size of one pixel.
structures.countTooltip: How many groups to cut the map into. Leave empty to let the data decide: the count rises while the group compositions stay distinguishable, and stops when they start duplicating each other.
structures.reclassifyHint: Both take effect on the next classification.
structures.nameTooltip: Put {{name}} on every pixel of this structure
structures.clearNameTooltip: Take the name off this structure; its pixels become unclassified
structures.mergeTooltip: Fold another structure into this one. The tool this data needs most: a small particle reads as a dilution gradient rather than a plateau, so it gets cut into concentric rings — on SampleB one Si particle became three structures at Si 24 / 36 / 52 at%. How much rim belongs to the particle is your call.
structures.splitTooltip: Re-group this structure's own pixels, leaving the rest of the map untouched. Raising the global count instead would re-cut every other structure too.
structures.growTooltip: Push this structure's edge out or pull it in by one pixel. Blind to the chemistry — use Snap for that.
structures.snapTooltip: Let every boundary relax onto the nearest strong chemistry edge. The slider is how wide a band around each boundary is put up for re-decision; the structures' interiors always keep their identity, so nothing can vanish or swap.
structures.handToolsHint: Naming a whole structure is one click. The hand tools are below for anything the grouping cannot express.
structures.handToolsTooltip: Rectangle, polygon, wand and map-wide replacement. These belong to the phase view; while grouping they are folded away so both toolsets do not compete for the same column.
structures.howStep1: 1 — The map is cut into STRUCTURES by element ratio alone. A structure is just "these pixels have the same chemistry"; it has no name yet, and its colour means nothing beyond telling it apart from its neighbours.
structures.howStep2: 2 — You give each structure a phase. Several structures may get the SAME phase — that is normal and expected, which is why one phase name appears on several rows in the list.
structures.howStep3: 3 — Switch to “Phases” to see the result: one colour per phase, so two neighbouring regions you gave the same phase become one uninterrupted area. Many structures, few phases.

inspector.title: Structure inspector
inspector.empty: Click a region on the map, or a row in the list, to inspect it.
inspector.headline: {{px}} px · {{pct}}% of the map
inspector.piecesTooltip: How many separate parts this structure is in, largest first. Three concentric rings of one particle show up here as three pieces of similar size — that is the sign to merge.
inspector.spreadTooltip: Standard deviation inside the structure. A structure that is not homogeneous is either two things or a gradient.
inspector.enrichmentTooltip: How many times the map's own background level this element reaches here. The same quantity the classifier gates on, so this readout and the classifier cannot disagree. Below about 1.3× the classifier itself cannot tell feature from background.
inspector.neighbourTooltip: Largest single-element difference: {{gap}} at%, over {{edge}} px of shared edge. Click to inspect it. A small gap on a long shared edge usually means one structure cut in two.
inspector.candidateTooltip: {{name}} is {{gap}} at% off on average. Click to put it on the whole structure.
inspector.compositionHint: Average of every pixel in this structure. ± is how much the pixels differ from that average — a large ± means the structure is not one thing.
inspector.neighboursHint: Structures this one borders on. The number is the biggest difference in any single element. A small number on a long border usually means one region got cut in two — merge it.
inspector.candidatesHint: Library phases sorted by how close their formula is to the measured composition. Click one to put it on the whole structure.
inspector.scaleLegend: vs background: 1.0× means this element is no more common here than anywhere else on the map. Above 1.3× it is genuinely concentrated here; below 0.8× it is depleted.

rollup.headline: {{structures}} structures → {{phases}} phases
rollup.explain: The list above names a phase once per structure, so a phase covering four structures is written four times. Here it is counted once.
rollup.unnamedTooltip: Structures with no phase yet. They are drawn as unclassified in the phase view.
rollup.showPhasesTooltip: One colour per phase. Neighbouring regions you gave the same phase become one uninterrupted area there.

tabs.elementsTooltip: The composite overlay, the layer stack and every element map side by side.
tabs.phaseMapTooltip: Group the map by chemistry into structures, then decide which phase each one is.
tabs.noMapYet: No phase map yet. Use Re-classify on the right to build one from the chemistry.
